title: The Gap
passages: Vey gripped the broken nib, its steel tip gleaming under the amber lamp. He didn't press the nib to the port yet. Instead, he slid his left hand into the slot, the one he'd kept hidden since the seventh line took his right. The bell began to pulse—a deep, tooth-rattling pressure that always meant a new writer was stealing the page. The amber light flared, and for the span of a single breath, the ledger's hand went slack. Vey's palm filled the void, tracing the mosaic of burned letters, feeling the steel yield just enough. A name slipped out clean, uncounted by the scrubbers, but the ledger didn't let go of the hand. Vey's fingers clenched around nothing, and the port hissed, registering a new cost. Down in the spine, Jax felt the valve give a half-millimeter, the needle groaning, but he held the wheel, teeth gritted, knowing one slip and the spine would bleed out into vacuum. The bell retracted, the hand snapped back, and Vey stood left-handed, the gap closed, the cost unpaid.

The silence after the bell was not empty. It was full of the next one, stacked behind the first like another card.

Vey did not put his hand back in the port. He pressed his palm to the cold steel instead, flat, no grip, no trace. Mara watched the seam of the slot. Jax watched the valve wheel, his bloody arm locked against the rail, the inked edge flaking. The needle above the spine held at the edge of red, and Jax’s breath had gone shallow around the wheel.

“You’re not signing,” Mara said.

“I’m negotiating,” Vey said.

“With who?”

The port didn’t answer. It never did. The ledger was all signal and appetite, and the bell was its appetite’s teeth.

Jax made a sound in his teeth, and Mara’s pen stopped mid-click. The scrubber readouts on the hatch were numbers she had stopped reading aloud; needle past red, registers dropping with each name collected. The crew had maybe minutes of air and one free name between them and the next strike.

Vey left his hand there, palm down, not signing. Ines, in the vent, felt the deck shudder and knew the spine was listening.
